intro: Malawi, the 'Warm Heart of Africa', is a narrow country along one of the world's great lakes.

chapters.title: The Maravi
text: The Maravi kingdoms ruled the region from the 1400s, and the country takes its name from them. In the 1800s Yao and Swahili-Arab traders ran a slave trade to the coast.

chapters.title: Nyasaland
text: David Livingstone campaigned against the slave trade here. Britain made it the protectorate of Nyasaland in 1891.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Malawi became independent in 1964 under Hastings Banda, who ruled as 'president for life' until multi-party elections in 1994. In 2020 judges overturned a flawed election, a first in Africa for a re-run that unseated the president.

highlight.title: Courts
highlight.text: Malawi's 2020 election re-run was hailed as a win for democracy.
